 Stock Market Today Live Updates: Sensex jumps over 900 points, Nifty50 adds 1% to rise above 25,200 
 LIVE NOW Save Share Comments Stock Market Today Live Updates: Sensex jumps over 900 points, Nifty50 adds 1% to rise above 25,200
 THE TIMES OF INDIA | Nov 11, 2026, 13:26:15 IST SUMMARY The outlook for the benchmark indices depends on a combination of domestic and global triggers. A sharp correction in crude oil prices, improving foreign fund flows and buying in banking and financial stocks have supported the recent rally in benchmark indices. 
 However, volatility in the oil market remains a key factor to watch, with hopes of de-escalation in the Iran conflict competing with concerns over attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Currency movements will also remain in focus, with the rupee having gained against the US dollar amid lower crude prices and improving foreign inflows. 
 Meanwhile, mixed global cues, US inflation data and developments in the artificial intelligence sector could influence the direction of international markets and investor sentiment. 
 Together, these factors are expected to shape the direction of stock market in the days ahead. Track TOI’s coverage on BSE Sensex and Nifty50 to know which way stock markets are headed: Live Events 
 13:25 (IST) Nov 11 Stock market today: BSE Sensex trads 900 points higher, Nifty50 above 25,250 Benchmark indices limited gains by afternoon, after opening 1% higher. BSE Sensex was trading 982.87 points, or 1.21% up at 82,089.52 while NSE Nifty50 advanced 240 points, or 0.96%, to 25,284.25. 12:00 (IST) Nov 11 BSE Sensex opens at an eight-month high 11:24 (IST) Nov 11 Stock market today: BSE Sensex trades over 1,200 points higher - check laggards on the index The BSE Sensex was trading at 82,378.65, up 1,272 points or 1.57%. Among the index's losers, Titan slipped 0.04% to Rs 5,002.90, while Sun Pharma declined 0.26% to Rs 1,900.00. 10:16 (IST) Nov 11 Stock market today: Top reasons why stock market is rallying 
 Dalal Street returned from its Diwali break in a cheerful mood on Wednesday, with benchmark indices climbing to levels last seen in February. Sensex jumped over 1,300 points during early trade, while Nifty 50 crossed the 25,300 mark as buying spread across sectors. Read full story › 09:42 (IST) Nov 11 Nifty 50 has surged by 8.6% in just six trading days of this month. This surge was triggered mainly by the aggressive FII buying of Rs 53170 crores so far this month. The dramatic change in the market environment was triggered by positive global cues for India from the weakening of the AI trade. But it is important to note that the real fundamental support to the rally has come from the better-than-expected Q2 results. The near 24% earnings growth in Nifty 50 in Q2 is a 12-quarter high and has compressed the forward PE for Nifty 50 to fair levels.
 V K Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist, Geojit Investments
 09:26 (IST) Nov 11 Stock market today: NSE Nifty50 adds 1% - check top gainers NSE Nifty50 advanced 319.65 points, or 1.28%, to 25,361.90 in early trade. IndiGo led early gainers on the index, rising Rs 225.60, or 4.15%, to Rs 5,655.60.
 Mahindra & Mahindra gained Rs 100.40, or 3.05%, to Rs 3,391, while Power Grid Corporation climbed Rs 5.30, or 2.05%, to Rs 263.25.
 State Bank of India advanced Rs 21, or 2.02%, to Rs 1,063, while Asian Paints rose Rs 47.70, or 1.90%, to Rs 2,557.

 IndiGo led the gainers, rising 4.33% to Rs 5,648. Mahindra & Mahindra followed with a 3.53% gain to Rs 3,400.05, while Asian Paints advanced 2.45% to Rs 2,563.10. Bharti Airtel climbed 2.29% to Rs 2,112.20, SBI gained 2.10% to Rs 1,063.35 and HDFC Bank rose 1.98% to Rs 811.85.
 09:18 (IST) Nov 11 Stock market today: Sensex opens over 1,000 points up, Nifty50 jumps 1% in opening trade Dalal Street began Wednesday on a strong note, with both benchmarks gaining over 1% in opening trade. BSE Sensex soared a whopping 1090.85 points or 1.34% to 82,197.50. NSE Nifty50 added 283.90 points or 1.13% to trade at 25,324.70. 09:14 (IST) Nov 11 Stock market today: Rupee opens 20 paise higher against US dollar Rupee began Wednesday on a strong note, rising 0.2% of 20 paise. The currency rose to 93.72 against the US dollar, compared with its previous close of 93.9275. 08:43 (IST) Nov 11 Stock market today: GIFT Nifty signals positive opening for Sensex, Nifty Benchmark indices are expected to open higher after the Diwali holiday break, supported by lower crude oil prices and strong foreign fund inflows. GIFT Nifty futures were trading at 25,334, indicating a positive start for the Nifty 50. The benchmark index had ended its previous trading session at 25,044.65, marking a closing high of more than eight months. Indian stock markets remained closed on Tuesday on account of Diwali. 
 The positive opening indication came after the Nifty 50 and BSE Sensex gained nearly 9% during November. Easing crude prices, strong domestic earnings and renewed foreign portfolio investor interest have been among the factors supporting the recent rally in Indian equities.
 08:42 (IST) Nov 11 Stock market today: Asian markets gain as Japan's Nikkei extends winning run Asian equities showed a mixed but broadly positive trend, with Japan's Nikkei 225 climbing for a third consecutive session as data and earnings reports revived some optimism around the artificial intelligence sector. The benchmark advanced 0.80% to 60,942.48 at the midday break, while the broader Topix gained 0.79% to 3,924.51. MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares also rose 0.2%, while South Korea's KOSPI gained 0.4%. China's blue-chip stocks, however, slipped 0.2%. 
 The gains came against the backdrop of weakness on Wall Street, where US stocks had declined following hotter-than-anticipated inflation data. The mixed performance across Asian markets highlighted the differing trends in regional equities, with Japanese and South Korean benchmarks gaining while Chinese blue chips remained under pressure.
 08:41 (IST) Nov 11 Stock market today: Oil prices hold firm near $90 per barrel mark Crude oil prices recovered on Wednesday after falling to two-month lows in the previous session, as the market weighed hopes of de-escalation in the Iran conflict against continuing attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude futures rose 71 cents, or 0.78%, to $92.20 per barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude gained 49 cents, or 0.57%, to $86.53 per barrel. Data from the Washington Institute for Near East Policy showed that 37 ships were attacked in the Strait of Hormuz and surrounding waterways in October, the highest monthly total since the war began. Another 10 attacks had been recorded in November. Videos posted on social media and verified by Reuters also showed a Navig8 tanker on fire near Oman's coast. The vessel was among three tankers hit on Sunday for allegedly using unauthorised routes through the strait, according to Iranian state broadcaster. 08:41 (IST) Nov 11 Rupee in focus: Currency ended previous session below 94 against US dollar amid easing egopolitical cues Rupee appreciated 24 paise to 93.74 against the US dollar in early trade in its previous session, supported by lower crude oil prices, improving foreign fund flows and hopes of de-escalation in the Middle East. In the interbank foreign exchange market, the domestic currency opened at around 93.85 before gaining ground to touch 93.74. This followed a 43-paise rally on Friday, when rupee settled at 93.98 against the US dollar. Forex traders said the overall outlook for the currency remained positive, with progress towards peace in the Middle East expected to reduce the risk premium in crude oil prices. Over the weekend, US President Donald Trump had indicated that fresh military strikes against Iran were highly unlikely if negotiations progressed and both sides reached a strong agreement. 08:40 (IST) Nov 11 Stock market recap: BSE Sensex, NSE Nifty50 end Monday in green Benchmarks extended their winning run after a sharp weekly rally, with buying in blue-chip banking and financial stocks and a correction in crude oil prices supporting the gains. BSE Sensex had surged 6,568.49 points, or 8.82%, in the previous week, while NSE Nifty advanced 1,977.25 points, or 8.57%.
 In the subsequent session on Monday, the 30-share Sensex climbed 107.25 points, or 0.13%, to settle at 81,106.65. It had touched an intraday high of 81,339.41, gaining 340.01 points, or 0.41%. The Nifty rose 58.25 points, or 0.23%, to close at 25,044.65.
 Among Sensex constituents, State Bank of India, Trent, Larsen & Toubro, NTPC, HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank were among the leading gainers. HCL Tech, Tata Steel, UltraTech Cement and Bajaj Finance, however, featured among the major laggards. Meanwhile, Brent crude declined 1.04% to $97.46 per barrel.
 Benchmark indices began Wednesday on a strong note, with BSE Sensex and NSE Nifty50 gaining 1% in early trading. Dalal Street is entering a crucial phase, with easing crude oil prices, renewed foreign investor buying and strong domestic earnings providing support to benchmark indices. Nifty 50 and Sensex have already gained nearly 9% in November, while foreign portfolio investors have pumped $5.68 billion into Indian equities, marking their biggest monthly buying since September 2024. 
However, developments in the Middle East, particularly attacks on shipping routes through the Strait of Hormuz, continue to keep crude oil prices in focus. 
Global cues also remain mixed, with inflation concerns in the US weighing on Wall Street even as Asian markets show resilience. The movement of crude prices, foreign flows and global technology stocks will remain important factors shaping market sentiment and the outlook ahead.
